Analysis: Both hypotheses present innovative dual-target strategies for overcoming immunosuppression in HCC by combining metabolic modulation with immune checkpoint blockade. Hypothesis 1 uses established methods (CRISPR/Cas9, selective inhibitors, and PD-1/PD-L1 blockade) to target HIF-1α and ENTPD2, yielding a concept that, while complex, is supported by more conventional therapeutic modalities. Its integration with checkpoint inhibitors adds plausibility and a clearer experimental framework, despite concerns with mechanistic details and off-target effects. Hypothesis 2 introduces additional novelty by targeting exosome-mediated ncRNA signaling and employing CRISPR/dCas9-based epigenetic silencing with nanocarrier delivery. However, this extra layer of novelty also heightens challenges in mechanistic clarity, delivery feasibility, and overall testability. Safety concerns around novel nanocarrier systems and epigenetic silencing further complicate its translational outlook. We therefore judge Hypothesis 1 as superior in balancing novelty with plausibility, testability, and safety.
